# Aftercare
## Monitored indicators
- oxygen, circulating blood, and perfusion; - pressure, heart rhythm, shock, and consciousness; - external and internal bleeding; - bandage saturation and contamination; - infection, necrosis, and scar state; - organ, bone, tendon, nerve, and joint function; - active drugs and toxic load; - power, heat, EMP, and cyberware neural link.
## After a bandage or hemostatic
1. Re-scan. 2. Check the change in external bleeding rate. 3. Monitor bandage saturation. 4. Once saturated, replace the item or perform vascular repair.
## After a tourniquet
1. Record the in-character application time. 2. Monitor limb ischemia. 3. Before removal, prepare wound control and blood. 4. Remove the tourniquet. 5. Check for bleeding return and the condition of distal areas.
## After transfusion
1. Re-scan blood and perfusion. 2. Check the compatibility response. 3. Make sure the active blood source is controlled.
## After surgery
1. Verify surgical access is closed. 2. Check external and internal bleeding. 3. Check the function of the operated organ or limb. 4. Check infection, contamination, and necrosis. 5. Check active drugs and toxic load. 6. Repeat a full scan after the state changes.
## IC patient handoff
Provide: injury mechanism and time, affected areas, active blood sources, tourniquet time, administered drugs, transfusions, completed surgical steps, installed graft or cyberware, and remaining restrictions.
